reports.publicQuestion: What is the lowest grade of students who do not have any friends?
allReplies: submit

FROM Highschooler h

reports.publicQuestion: Show the ids of high schoolers who have friends and are also liked by someone else.
reports.contractText: {"output_columns":[{"attribute_phrase":"ids of high schoolers","semantic_owner":"Highschooler","schema_expression":"Highschooler.ID"}],"row_constraints":["high schooler has at least one friend (appears as student_id in Friend)","high schooler is liked by someone else (appears as liked_id in Likes)"],"grouping":["one row per qualifying Highschooler entity (distinct ID)"],"ordering":[],"selected_role_check":"JOIN_CARDINALITY: Friend and Likes can each have multiple rows per student, so joining both directly would multiply rows; use EXISTS subqueries (or DISTINCT) to test existence without row multiplication, and verify join keys are student_id/friend_id and student_id/liked_id per schema."}
allReplies:
SELECT DISTINCT h.ID
FROM Highschooler h
JOIN Friend f ON h.ID = f.student_id
JOIN Likes l ON h.ID = l.liked_id;
submit

{"output_columns":[{"attribute_phrase":"ids of high schoolers","semantic_owner":"Highschooler","schema_expression":"Highschooler.ID"}],"row_constraints":["high schooler has at least one friend (appears as student_id in Friend)","high schooler is liked by someone else (appears as liked_id in Likes)"],"grouping":["one row per qualifying Highschooler entity (distinct ID)"],"ordering":[],"selected_role_check":"JOIN_CARDINALITY: Friend and Likes can each have multiple rows per student, so joining both directly would multiply rows; use EXISTS subqueries (or DISTINCT) to test existence without row multiplication, and verify join keys are student_id/friend_id and student_id/liked_id per schema."}

SELECT DISTINCT h.ID
FROM Highschooler h
WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Friend f WHERE f.student_id = h.ID)
  AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Likes l WHERE l.liked_id = h.ID);

A LEFT JOIN would be needed only if documents with zero paragraphs must be shown; the question asks for the number of paragraphs in each document, and grouping by Document_ID with COUNT over the joined rows yields the paragraph count per document."}

FROM Documents d
LEFT JOIN Paragraphs p ON d.Document_ID = p.Document_ID
GROUP BY d.Document_ID
ORDER BY d.Document_ID;

reports.publicQuestion: Find all airlines that have flights from airport 'CVO' but not from 'APG'.

allReplies:

FROM flights
WHERE SourceAirport = 'CVO'
AND Airline NOT IN (
    SELECT Airline
    FROM flights
    WHERE SourceAirport = 'APG'
)

reports.publicQuestion: Find the number of cities in each district whose population is greater than the average population of cities?
reports.contractText: {"output_columns":[{"attribute_phrase":"number of cities","semantic_owner":"district","schema_expression":"COUNT(city.ID)"},{"attribute_phrase":"district","semantic_owner":"district","schema_expression":"city.District"}],"row_constraints":["city population is greater than the average population of cities"],"grouping":["group by city.District"],"ordering":[],"selected_role_check":"JOIN_CARDINALITY: The query uses a single table (city) with no joins, so no join cardinality or row-multiplication risk exists; COUNT(city.ID) counts qualifying cities per district without needing DISTINCT."}
allReplies:
SELECT District, COUNT(*) AS city_count
FROM city
WHERE Population > (SELECT AVG(Population) FROM city)
GROUP BY District;
submit

{"output_columns":[{"attribute_phrase":"number of cities","semantic_owner":"district","schema_expression":"COUNT(city.ID)"},{"attribute_phrase":"district","semantic_owner":"district","schema_expression":"city.District"}],"row_constraints":["city population is greater than the average population of cities"],"grouping":["group by city.District"],"ordering":[],"selected_role_check":"JOIN_CARDINALITY: The query uses a single table (city) with no joins, so no join cardinality or row-multiplication risk exists; COUNT(city.ID) counts qualifying cities per district without needing DISTINCT."}

SELECT District, COUNT(ID) AS city_count
FROM city
WHERE Population > (SELECT AVG(Population) FROM city)
